name: Hydrogen
description: Hydrogen's main state at any resonable temperature is gaseous. It only becomes a liquid at -240.21°C. If you lick it at that temperature, not only will you be the first person to lick Hydrogen, you will also freeze your tounge off. However, everything else would be A-OK.

name: Helium
description: Helium is a gas. You can't lick it at any temperature above -270°C, where it then becomes a solid. But at that point you freeze your tounge off. Congrats. Your voice would be a little squeaky though.

name: Lithium
description: Lithium is that acid stuff in coin batteries. Licking it would cause a burn on your tounge, wouldn't taste good, and is bad for your insides if it makes it all the way down.

name: Beryllium
description: Beryllium isn't your friend. Inhaling it (which you probably would do if you were to lick it) can lead to many bad things, even Lung Cancer. It also would burn your tounge. Other than that you are good to go!

name: Boron
lick: Yeah, just don't lick too much.
description: Boron is one of those things that one lick won't hurt, but a lot of licks can cause kidney failure and similar stuff. However, one lick won't really hurt you.

name: Carbon
description: Carbon is 100% safe to lick. (Ever lick the tip of your pencil?)

name: Nitrogen
description: Nitrogen is a gas, so you can't technically lick it unless it is really, really cold (at which point you would freeze your tounge off) but other than the missing tounge you would be fine.

name: Oxygen
description: Oxygen is super, duper common. Without it we would die. However, it is a gas, so good luck "licking" it.

name: Fluorine
description: Fluorine is highly reactive and will burn you badly. Its also a gas, so you would probably inhale it when trying to lick it, which is really bad.

name: Neon
description: It's a gas, so you would have to figure out how to lick a gas, but once you figure that out, you will learn it is harmless.

name: Sodium
description: When sodium touches water, it can fizz, burst into flames, and explode. Not good. Just look up "Sodium + Water" on YouTube. Now imagine that happening on your TOUNGE...

name: Magnesium
description: Magnesium is perfectly fine to lick. Some people actually take magnesium pills.

name: Aluminium
description: Aluminium is super common. From foil to soda cans. If you have ever had a Pepsi or similar, you probably already have licked it!

name: Silicon
description: Small amounts of it is fine, which is what you would get if you were to lick it.

name: Phosphorus
description: Phosphorus isn't your friend. When exposed to air, it catches fire. It also is poisonus, so if you were to get it into your mouth without it blowing up, you would still die.

name: Sulfur
description: It isn't bad for you, it isn't good for you either. So yes, you can lick it and not be harmed, but WHY?

name: Chlorine
description: If you have ever been in a swimming pool, you have probably taken in some chlorine, however, raw chlorine would probably hurt your tounge.

name: Argon
description: Argon is a gas, so you can't get a solid state of it easily, but if somehow you could lick a gas, it would be fine.

name: Potassium
description: Potassium reacts very viloently when it comes into contact with water. Since your mouth has water in it, potassium would react viloently with your MOUTH. That wouldn't be good.

name: Calcium
description: Calcium + the Air = bad stuff. Calcium + your tounge = really bad stuff.

name: Scandium
description: Scandium is one of those rare things. You could lick it and come away from it fine, but good luck finding it.

name: Titanium
description: Titanium is a metal, like steel! It wouldn't hurt a fly (probably).

name: Vanadium
description: Vanadium is in various foods, but in REALLY small amounts. So one lick will be fine.

name: Chromium
description: Chromium comes in various forms. For example, Chromium-6 is bad for you, but Chromium-3 is fine in small amounts. So just make sure you know what you are licking.

name: Manganese
description: In small amounts, it is fine (like in really small amounts). But too much can lead to Parkinson's Disease-Like systems. (BADDDD).

name: Iron
description: Iron is fine to lick. Need I say more?

name: Cobalt
description: Cobalt is fine in small amounts, but it you have too much, it can lead to bad stuff.

name: Nickel
description: Nickel is fine to lick a few times.

_COMMENT: Make a small note in UI saying they can't sue (as a joke of course)
name: Copper
description: Copper is totally okay to lick. I dare you to do it.

name: Zinc
description: People often take some zinc supplements, and they are fine (i think) so licking it can't hurt.

name: Gallium
description: Gallium is just another boring metal. Fun fact: it has a really low melting point! Who knew!

name: Germanium
description: Germainium is totally fine to lick. It is like silicon.

name: Arsenic
description: Arsenic is poison. Please don't attempt to lick it. It won't end very well.

name: Selenium
description: One lick won't hurt. However, if you have 900-1000 micrograms per day, you can lose your hair and nails...

name: Bromine
description: Bromine, a liquid at room temperature, can cause irritation to the skin, vomiting, and more. If exposed, The CDC recommends you take off your clothes. Their words, not mine.

name: Krypton
lick: Yes if you can find it!
description: (not to be confused with Kryptonite) Krypton is a super rare gas found in the atmosphere, lightning, and other small things. It is non-toxic and won't hurt you if you somehow lick it.

name: Rubidium
description: Rubidium reacts harshly with water and air, so by the time it got to your tounge it would be on fire, and from there your day would go downhill.

name: Strontium
description: Strontium can be found in a variety of things, including some toothpaste! So there is a chance you have already licked it!

name: Yttrium
description: Yttrium is rare and is found in LEDs and some cancer medicine! A lick should be okay.

name: Zirconium
description: Zirconium is a rare metal that is fine to lick. Nothing else to say.

name: Niobium
description: Niobium is really strong and can take a lot of heat. You can lick it. It is actually used in jewelry.
